topic: F04 discrepancy resolution, F06 session-aware robustness battery, F06/F07 candidate atlases, and multimodal substrate verification

count_7_of_139.target: Binary expected omission identity (A vs B) during omitted slot (p2, p3, p4)
count_7_of_139.model: Linear SVC (C=1.0) with balanced training classes per fold
count_7_of_139.null: Within-cycle label permutation (100 permutations per cell)
count_7_of_139.result: 7 / 139 cells (5.04%) nominally significant at p < 0.05 (exactly equal to alpha = 0.05 chance rate); 0 / 139 survive Benjamini-Hochberg FDR

count_3_of_139.target: 3-way expected omission identity (A vs B vs R) during omitted slot (p2, p3, p4) [Y_omit]
count_3_of_139.model: Multinomial Logistic Regression (C=1.0) with balanced training classes per fold
count_3_of_139.null: Within-cycle label permutation (100 permutations per cell)
count_3_of_139.result: 3 / 139 cells (2.16%) nominally significant at p < 0.05 (at or below alpha = 0.05 chance rate); 0 / 139 survive Benjamini-Hochberg FDR

f04_provenance_resolution.conclusion: 7/139 estimates binary linear-SVM classification balanced accuracy under within-cycle permutation, whereas 3/139 estimates 3-way multinomial logistic regression log-loss under within-cycle permutation across the identical 139 session x area x slot cells; therefore they are NOT estimating the identical mathematical quantity, but both consistently establish that omission identity cannot be decoded above chance from spiking activity under leakage-safe cross-validation.
